newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN reports on Iraqi oil sale arrangements in place.
newsitem.headline: UN reports on Iraqi oil sale arrangements in place.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali reported Wednesday that most of the arrangements required for the oil-for-food deal with Iraq were now in place.

In a 50-page report to the Security Council, he outlined how the plan would work but did not state when he would give the go-ahead to implement the deal which allows Iraq to sell $2 billion oil in order to purchase food, medicine and other goods.
"Most of the arrangements required to bring resolution 986 into effect are today in place," he said, referring to the council's 1995 resolution that set up the plan.
The council is not expected to discuss the plan immediately.

Boutros-Ghali said that he would have to submit another report that would trigger the final go-ahead at a minute after midnight New York time, the day after the council president informs the 15-member body he has received it.
He said the pricing mechanism formula for the export of Iraqi oil had been sent to the Security Council's sanctions committee and if no member objects, it would be approved.
The United States, which previously delayed approval, has said it would not block the formula this month. No meeting is scheduled on Wednesday by the committee to approve the formula.

In the report, Boutros-Ghali confirmed 14 oil monitors would be sent to Baghdad, 4 at the Ceyhan terminal, 4 at the metering stations on the Kirkuk-Yumurtalik pipeline at the border between Iraq and Turkey and 6 at Mina al-Bakr in the Gulf.

He said there was no problem with the Mina al-Bakr terminal but the metering station at Zakho at the border between Iraq and Turkey needed some technical work and spare parts were needed. He said he had been told by Iraq that the spare parts were located and work was underway to upgrade the equipment.
The Saybolt firm of the Netherlands is expected to inspect the equipment again early in December.
On humanitarian goods, the United Nations is launching a large team of more than 150 people to monitor how the food and other necessities are being distributed.
